chose: index CATCHES Unrunnable from the structural diff and files it as an unread source, instead of letting cli.ts's total handler abort the run
over: letting the CLI's uncaughtException renderer take it, as log and signal do
pre-checking for a git repo before calling graphAtRef
because: cli.ts's total Unrunnable handler is the right answer for a command whose WHOLE JOB needs history (log, signal): it exits 2 with a sentence. The Index has three views and only one of them reads history, so aborting would cost the reader the map and the journal because git was unavailable — a shallow CI clone or a source export is an ordinary consumer, not an exotic state. A pre-check would be floor.ts's rejected shape (a second spelling of the requirement, one per caller). Catching the typed throw keeps the requirement stated once at the seam that discovers it, and the page then says WHICH source it lost and why — which is the same doctrine, applied at a page instead of at a process.

chose: unvisited = paths in the recent concern band that the graph does not own — the complement of economy's closure, not a new churn statistic
over: files with churn that appear in zero reading closures (identical set, computed the expensive way)
because: closureOf returns NULL for a commit touching nothing the graph owns, so a path outside the graph can never enter a closure by construction — the two candidate definitions denote the same set and the cheap one reuses fileChurn + the graph's file nodes with no second history read. It measures 173/274 on the consuming project and 72/165 here, which is the finding: most of what recent work touches is invisible to every read-cost figure the harness prints. Denominator is the distinct paths the 2..BULK band touched; with no git it is UNMEASURED, never 0.
